$comment: Colour catalog for the `og agents` pane. A theme entry is a row here, not
code -- same rule as registry.json.
label    what the picker shows (exact display name)
order    picker's sort key; the row order the operator's reference site
(ansicolor.com) lists its 25 themes in
colors   seven roles, lowercase #rrggbb, no shorthand, no alpha:
bg       pane background
text     dominant body text -- agent and worker names
meta     secondary text -- model ids, timestamps, status detail
sel_bg   background of the SELECTED row
idle     idle status glyph (check mark)
working  working status glyph (spinner)
rail     group rails and box-drawing borders
Every value is the theme's own published colour (upstream theme file or
terminal port), NOT generated from one formula -- Nord reads as Nord,
Gruvbox as Gruvbox. tests/test_og_themes_catalog.py recomputes WCAG
contrast over all 25 and fails the build if the pane is unreadable, so a
new row added here must clear: text/bg >= 4.5, text/sel_bg >= 4.5,
meta/bg, idle/bg, working/bg >= 3.0, rail/bg >= 1.5.
AND THE SAME FLOORS AGAIN ON THE RESOLVED 256-COLOUR CELL, because that
is what paints. On the terminal this ships to -- TERM=tmux-256color, so
curses.COLORS is 256 and init_color does not exist -- a hex is quantised to
one of the 240 palette cells, and a theme can clear every floor above on
paper and still paint under it. A colour that carries chroma may never
resolve to a neutral cell (installer/og_themes.py refuses it): 52 roles
across 23 of the 25 themes used to lose their chroma to the greyscale ramp,
so Nord and Solarized Dark and every Catppuccin lavender rendered as grey.
Where a theme's published foreground cannot reach its target, that single
value is nudged in LIGHTNESS ONLY (hue and saturation untouched), by the
minimum amount that clears the target. Nudges are listed in the test file,
with the ones the CELLS demanded marked post-conversion.
THE EXCEPTION IS `og`, WHICH IS NOT A THEME BUT TODAY. It is what this pane
painted before themes existed, and it is the only row here whose values were
not chosen: they were READ OFF the code. Its order is 0 so the picker sorts
it FIRST -- dracula stays the default, and `og` is the way back, not the way
in. Four of its seven roles are the string "default", which means curses -1:
allocate no colour and inherit the terminal's own. That is the whole of the
row. The pane used to allocate every pair with a -1 background ("what lets
colour and the pane's transparency coexist"), and dracula's opaque background
ends that; `og` is the only way to get it back, which makes it the
REGRESSION GUARD for the whole background change rather than a cosmetic
extra. Its three hexes are the exact sRGB of the indices the code shipped --
#87afaf is ansi 109, #00ff00 is 46, #ffff00 is 226 -- and a test asserts the
round trip, so this row is provably today's colours and not an approximation
of them. Do not give it invented hexes to make it measurable; see the
exemption in the test file.

og.label: OG
og._note: NOT a theme: today's colours, preserved as a choice. bg/text/sel_bg/rail are 'default' (curses -1, the terminal's own background) because that is exactly what the pane painted before themes existed. The three hexes are the exact sRGB of the indices the code shipped and are EXEMPT from every contrast assertion in tests/test_og_themes_catalog.py -- 'default' has no computable luminance, so a contrast test over this row crashes or silently skips, and inventing hexes to satisfy one would destroy the only property this row exists for.

dracula.label: Dracula
dracula._note: text is #ffd7af, a warm parchment, and it was CHOSEN BY THE OPERATOR from the 256-colour palette cells -- not read off Dracula's upstream theme, and not a nudge of one. It is deliberately NEITHER Dracula's own Parchment #f8f8f2 NOR the #f0e6d2 this row used to ship. The reason it is not #f0e6d2 is a BUG, not a taste: #f0e6d2's nearest 256-colour cell is 254, a PURE GREY, so on any terminal reporting 256 colours -- every terminal that does not claim truecolor, tmux included -- the default pane painted its body text grey where parchment was asked for. The converter no longer does that (installer/og_themes.py: a chromatic colour may not resolve to a neutral cell), and #ffd7af is what the operator picked from the cells that remain. #ffd7af IS ansi 223 exactly -- it is a cube cell, so the round trip is lossless and asserted in tests/test_og_themes.py -- it is the closest in lightness of the candidates shown, and it sits 17.9 degrees of hue from the original parchment, which is why the brighter 230 and the more muted 187 were not chosen. Do not 'correct' it back to Dracula's #f8f8f2 and do not 'correct' it to #f0e6d2: neither is what was chosen, and only one of the two survives conversion at all.
